title: Sustainability and Resources
summary: Examine electricity, water, land, equipment life, and efficiency as connected design considerations.
objectives: Name several resources a data-center design uses or affects.
Explain why sustainability decisions involve tradeoffs and evidence.

vocab.def: Planning to meet needs while considering effects over time.
Something a system uses, such as energy, water, land, or materials.
The stages from creating and using something through reuse or disposal.

sections.heading: Resources are part of infrastructure
sections.body: A design may use electricity, water where applicable, land, building materials, network equipment, and cooling resources. Equipment also has a lifecycle that includes maintenance, reuse, and disposal.

sections.heading: Efficiency is not the only question
sections.body: Using less of one resource may affect reliability, cost, or another resource. A thoughtful team asks what evidence supports a choice and who may experience its effects.

sections.heading: Make a balanced comparison
sections.body: Compare two conceptual designs and list an energy benefit, a land or water question, and an information gap for each. Do not reduce sustainability to a simple yes or no.

practice.prompt: A design uses less land but more cooling energy. What tradeoff does that create, and what additional evidence would help the team decide?

quiz.question: Why should a design consider equipment lifecycle?
options: Materials and waste matter before, during, and after use
Lifecycle replaces the need for security
quiz.answer: Materials and waste matter before, during, and after use

reflectionPrompt: Which resource question should a community ask about a large infrastructure design?
